title: The exported deformation film shows both sheets, but its caption says nothing about sheets and calls the root path the principal branch
detail: This is the user's own case: chain √ then sin, √ bracketed, Landscape, All sheets, deformation open. Export figure then defaults to the four-panel film (a) t=0 … (d) t=1, and each panel draws both sheets of H_t; panel (d) shows ±sin √z crossing. The caption is word for word the one exported with All sheets off. It reads: 'Landscapes of $H_t$ … the height is Im H_t and the color shows arg H_t. Here H_t=f_2∘G_t … G_t is the homotopy G_t(z)=z^{1-(1/2)t} (principal branch).' So the caption names one branch for a figure that draws two. Every deforming case with All sheets falls into this film caption, so none of them gets a sheets clause: whole-chain sin √z, log z, ∛z, ⁵√ then ⁶√, √ then log. EN and RU are the same ('(главная ветвь)', no clause). The new sheetsClause reaches only the single-frame landscape caption (figure.js ~2271). The film branch (figure.js ~2227, fi.film === 'land') never calls it. This is exactly the user's point 4: an exported caption that does not say exactly what is drawn.
evidence: notes/v16-user5/review-user/film-sinsqrt.png (All sheets on: two surfaces in (b)-(d)) next to film-sinsqrt-nosheets.png (off: one surface). The two captions are identical. All captions: notes/v16-user5/review-user/captions-c1.json, cases sinsqrt-br, sinsqrt-whole, log-def, cube-def, capped-def, sqrt-then-log-def (EN, RU, and the figure's own caption). 1440×900, light, work/xvta dist/test.html, __cmwFig.build({for:'article'}).
fix: In figure.js, in the fi.film === 'land' caption: when c.sheets && c.sheets.hom, append the same clause as the single frame, A.sheetsClause(c.sheets, 'tex', c.Fname), with H and F as math. In homDef / the film's homotopy sentence, do not write '(principal branch)' for a deformed root, power or log while sheets are drawn. Say instead that the path is taken on each sheet ('on every sheet' / 'на каждом листе'), or leave the branch remark out. Add the film case to export_cmd.js section 6, which tests only static cases and one single-frame deformation.

title: The on-screen and single-frame captions contradict themselves while deforming with All sheets
detail: In the user's case, the screen caption (__cmwCapText) says 'the sheets of $H_t$ that become the sheets of $F$ are shown.' A sentence later it says 'G_t is the homotopy G_t(z)=z^{1-(1/2)t} (principal branch)'. The reader is told two sheets are drawn and that the map is the principal branch. The deformation's definition sentence comes from the same homotopy text as with All sheets off.
evidence: Output of __cmwCapText() in Landscape, √ bracketed, All sheets, deformation at t=1. The text is quoted in this review's run, s3 step. Screenshot: notes/v16-user5/review-user/s3-grid.png.
fix: Same root cause as user-1. When sheetsShown().hom, the homotopy sentence should drop '(principal branch)' or say the path runs on each sheet. Then check that both screen and LaTeX read consistently in EN and RU.

title: While deforming, the pane title and the All sheets check count F's sheets, not the surfaces actually drawn
detail: The landscape draws only the sheets of the steps already begun ('a step not begun adds its sheets when it starts'). The Landscape title and the check label still give F's full count. Whole chain ⁵√z then ⁶√, one after another, mid-deformation: 5 surfaces are drawn, but the title reads 'landscape of Im H_t, 24 of 30 sheet combinations' and the check reads 'All sheets (24 of 30)', with the tip '24 of the 30 surfaces are drawn'. √z then log z: 2 surfaces drawn, title '…, 10 sheets, k = −2…2'. The user asked for wording that is exactly true. A tip that says '24 … are drawn' while 5 are drawn is false.
evidence: notes/v16-user5/review-user/captions-c1.json: capped-def has drawn.K=5 and shown.K=24; sqrt-then-log-def has drawn.K=2 and shown.K=10. Fields 'title' and 'tip'.
fix: While hom, build the title suffix and the check's tip from render3D.sheetsInfo (the K actually drawn at this t). Alternatively, phrase it as F's sheets, e.g. ', on F's 24 of 30 sheet combinations', and change the tip to say those are F's counts. Do the same for the single-frame LaTeX clause when the drawn K is below F's.

title: Tour 'Cauchy integral' asks the user to select another closed curve, but lights nothing and the scene has no other closed curve
detail: Body: 'Select another closed curve to use it instead.' The step lights only the phase-style row and the panes. The Shapes list and the Select tool are not lit, and no drawing tool is lit either. The scene's z-plane has a single closed curve (Circle 1, |z|=1), so the user would first have to draw one, and nothing tells them how. This is the user's point 1: a task involving the left panel with no tool lit. The v16.1 audit lists cauchy as 'only describes', so its control table (CTL) never checks it.
evidence: notes/v16-user5/review-user/tour-1440-cauchy.png (1440, light, EN, mouse): the Shapes list has only Circle 1, and the left panel is dimmed. notes/v16-user5/review-user/tour-walk-1440.json, row analysis/cauchy: ctl=[] (nothing checked).
fix: Either drop the sentence, or make it a real task. For the task: add a second closed curve to the 'cauchy' scene (e.g. |z-0.5|=1.2), give the step try { text: 'Click the other circle.', ctl: ['tool:select'] } with ['tool','select'] in before, and light the Shapes list row. Add the step to the audit's CTL table.

title: The two sheets can be seen coming apart, but they are hard to tell apart near t=0, and comb edges dominate the early frames
detail: On sin(√z) with √ bracketed, Landscape, All sheets, the deformation draws two surfaces at every t, on desktop and on a phone (390, dark). At t=0 they coincide (sin z), as expected. By t≈0.3 they are clearly apart, and at t=1 they are ±sin √z. So the user can see two sheets merge into one by playing it backwards. At t≤0.15, though, the two surfaces interpenetrate with the same phase colours, and the saturated clamp walls show saw-tooth combs (also in the exported film, panels (a) and (b)). A reader cannot easily tell which surface is which sheet. The combs are not new: the same chain with All sheets off shows them too.
evidence: notes/v16-user5/review-user/s3-grid.png (1440, light; t=0, 0.15, 0.3, 0.5, 0.75, 1), s3-T0.15.png, p1-grid.png (390×844, dark, touch; t=0.05, 0.3, 1). film-sinsqrt.png against film-sinsqrt-nosheets.png for the combs.
fix: Optional, and for the user to decide: a per-sheet cue (a slight tint or a thin seam line on sheet k≠0) so that the merge reads at small t. Separately, the comb edges at the height clamp are a known renderer limitation, worth an item on the backlog (article-grade rule).

title: The tour step and the guide still say All sheets draws 'the whole Riemann surface'
detail: The export captions are now exact. The tour step 'All sheets' still says 'In Landscape, All sheets draws the whole Riemann surface of a multivalued map: Im log z climbs a helicoid', but for log it draws k=−2…2. The reference guide says the same: 'All sheets draws its whole Riemann surface'. This is the same inexactness the user objected to for infinitely many sheets. It is not in the LaTeX, so it is outside the literal request, and the export piece left it on purpose.
fix: Reword both, e.g. 'draws the sheets of a multivalued map, a window of them when there are infinitely many: here Im log z climbs a helicoid …'. Add the Russian strings to notes/i18n/ru/v161-user5.json (read-modify-write).

title: On a phone, nothing on screen says which sheets are drawn
detail: At 390 px the Landscape pane has no title row, so 'both sheets' / 'sheets k = −2…2' never shows. The only sign is the check inside the Display sheet. The user tests on an Android phone and asked to see the sheets. They can see the surfaces, but not how many of them are drawn.
evidence: notes/v16-user5/review-user/p1-grid.png (390×844, dark, touch). __cmwLandSheets().title holds ', both sheets', but it is not displayed.
fix: Optional. Show the suffix in the phone's landscape hint chip or legend chip (e.g. 'Im H_t · both sheets'). Keep it inside the existing chip so that nothing new covers the work area.

title: Verified OK: exact tool lighting, pictures on the cards step, and Export menus over the dialog
detail: Tour, walked step by step with the audit's own probe, in 3 configs: 1440 light EN mouse with Names, 390 dark RU touch, and 1024 light EN touch with Names. Every task control was lit within 0.75 px: Disc, Select, 3 points, Line, Phase, Stretch, Landscape, Split, the slider of a, Play and t, card f₁ and f₂, All sheets, Copy LaTeX. On a phone the More tools sheet opens with the 3 points and Line tiles lit, and the Display sheet opens with All sheets lit. The cards step showed 3 card pictures every time and added the note 'The tour turns the cards' pictures on…'. The user's setting was restored after Next, after Esc, and after a reload mid-step, both from Names and from a chain dragged to 113 px. A Names choice made during the step stayed. Export figure: More formats and Size open over the dialog (z 55), are hit-tested at their centre and corners, sit inside the viewport, and take focus. Esc closes the menu, keeps the dialog and returns focus. Checked at 1440 light EN, 1440 dark RU, 1024 touch, 390 dark EN, 390 light RU and 844×390. The dialog's other popups are native selects. No exceptions.
